hypothesis.title: Instrument why prefix depth saturates at 5 before adding more scheduler knobs
hypothesis.description: Add a diagnostic dump (behind explore flag --depth-census, in spur-core/src/simulator/explorer.rs + path.rs) that, for runs reaching depth 3-5, records the event class actually taken at each frontier step and the set of enabled-but-unchosen classes. Emit a histogram to the run summary alongside depthAtLeast. No policy change, no config param: pure observability, evaluated by inspecting the histogram rather than by ladder deltas. Answers whether depth>=6 is unreachable (no enabled event extends the prefix), rarely-selected (enabled but low probability under any queue policy), or grader-truncated.
hypothesis.rationale: Two consecutive queue-priority hypotheses (counter-based and state-based) both returned exact nulls at depth>=6/7/8, with maxPrefixDepth pinned at 5 across every seed. That pattern says the ceiling is structural, not a matter of which queue we prefer. Further blind scheduler knobs will keep sampling the same null; a census tells us which of the three failure modes to attack and retires an entire branch of the pool.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Counts event classes at the exploration frontier using the simulator's own enabled-set, reading no protocol-specific state or VR message names; applies to any spec the explorer runs.
hypothesis.notes: [unparked iteration 50] Down-scored: partially redundant with end-run-at-plan-stall's diagnosis and depth-tail-power-analysis, but the enabled-but-unchosen census is distinct; falsified if the histogram shows frontier steps have no enabled extending event, which would make it a spec/grader limit and kill every queue-policy proposal.

reasons: meta changes require human review in v1
